front.title: JSON Meta Application Protocol (JMAP) Email Delivery Push Notifications

abstract.t: This document specifies an extension to the JSON Meta Application Protocol (JMAP) that allows clients to receive an object via a JMAP push subscription whenever a new email is delivered that matches a client-defined filter. The object can also include properties from the email, to allow a user notification to be displayed without having to make a further network request. Clients can also receive an object whenever a count of the emails in a chosen mailbox changes, for example to set a badge on an app icon.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: The JSON Meta Application Protocol (JMAP) defines a mechanism for creating a push subscription, allowing a client to be efficiently notified whenever the state on the server changes for a data type the client is interested in. This can be used to trigger a resync of that data in the client.

Many email clients wish to show the user a notification when a new email arrives. Email clients implementing JMAP for Mail may subscribe to changes in the pseudo-type "EmailDelivery" to be notified only when a new email is delivered (as opposed to whenever changes are made to the Email data in general, which may be caused by user actions such as reading, organising, or deleting their mail). However, this does not meet the needs of some email clients in constrained environments, particularly on mobile:

ol.li: Data is pushed for all email deliveries, but the client needs to receive them only when a message arrives for which it intends to show the user a notification. For example, notifications are commonly only shown for messages delivered to the inbox by default, not messages filtered to other mailboxes.

The client needs to make at least one HTTP request, and sometimes more, to resynchronise its datastore before it can show a visible notification to the user. This can sometimes fail when there is poor connectivity. In such circumstances, the client is only able to tell the user a new message has arrived, not any of the details such as who sent it, or the subject.

section.t: To address these issues, this document defines a way to receive a new EmailPush object via the JMAP push subscription. Clients can request a filter be applied to precisely restrict which messages they are notified about. Clients may request certain properties of the emails be included in the EmailPush object, so it has sufficient information to show the user notifications without having to make any further requests to the server.

Many clients also display a badge on their app icon, showing for example the number of unread emails in the inbox. This count changes not only when new email is delivered, but also when the user reads, moves, or deletes email, perhaps on another device. Keeping the badge accurate would require the client to resynchronise every time the mailbox changes, which has the same problems as described above. This document therefore also defines a way to receive a new EmailCount object via the JMAP push subscription whenever one of the counts of a single mailbox changes. Only the counts defined for the Mailbox object in are supported: these are generally kept up to date by the server anyway, whereas evaluating an arbitrary query every time the mailbox changes would be too expensive.

section.name: Notational Conventions
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.
Type signatures, examples, and property descriptions in this document follow the conventions established in .

section.name: Terminology
section.t: The same terminology is used in this document as in the core JMAP specification, see .
The term Email (with this specific capitalisation) is used to refer to the data type defined in .
Long lines in examples are wrapped as described in .

section.name: Addition to the Capabilities Object
section.t: The capabilities object is returned as part of the JMAP Session object; see . This document defines an additional capability URI.

section.name: urn:ietf:params:jmap:emailpush
section.t: The urn:ietf:params:jmap:emailpush capability adds support for the extensions to PushSubscription described in this document. The value of this property in the JMAP Session "capabilities" property is an empty object.
Accounts for which email delivery push is supported MUST have this capability in the account's "accountCapabilities" property. The value is an object with the following properties:

dl.dd: The list of FilterCondition property names the server supports in the "filter" of an EmailPushConfig for this account (see ). If null, the server supports all FilterCondition properties defined in , plus any defined in other JMAP extensions that the server supports for the "Email/query" method in this account.

The maximum depth of nested FilterOperator objects the server supports in the "filter" of an EmailPushConfig for this account. A filter that is a single FilterCondition has a depth of 0; a FilterOperator whose "conditions" are all FilterCondition objects has a depth of 1; each further level of nested FilterOperator adds 1 to the depth. This MUST be at least 1. If null, there is no limit on the depth.

The list of Mailbox count property names the server supports in the "property" of an EmailCountConfig for this account (see ). This is a subset of "totalEmails", "unreadEmails", "totalThreads", and "unreadThreads". If null, all four are supported. If the empty array, the server does not support EmailCount pushes for this account. If the urn:ietf:params:jmap:mail capability is supported for the account, this MUST be null.

section.t: Note, this capability may be supported in servers or accounts that do not support the urn:ietf:params:jmap:mail capability — in such cases, notification of new emails is supported but any further interaction will require use of a different protocol, such as IMAP .

section.name: The EmailPush Object
section.t: An EmailPush object represents one or more new messages that have been delivered to an account. A message is considered delivered under the same conditions that cause a change to the "EmailDelivery" type, as described in : when a new Email is added to the account via SMTP or another mail delivery mechanism, but not when it is created as the result of a JMAP method call or the equivalent in another protocol (such as an IMAP APPEND).
An EmailPush object has the following properties:

dl.dd: The id of the Account these Emails are in.

dd.t: An array of objects representing the new messages. Each object has the properties of the Email object (as defined in ) that were requested by the client in the EmailPushConfig. If multiple emails arrive in quick succession, or the server comes back online after a period of downtime, the server may include multiple Email objects in this array to reduce the number of push notifications it sends, avoiding rate limiting issues.

Note, push services often have strict restrictions on the size of data that can be sent. A push service is only required to support payloads of up to 4096 octets (see ), and the encryption defined in reduces the space available for the EmailPush object further. The server MUST NOT exceed the size limit of the push service; if multiple Email objects would not fit in a single EmailPush, the server MUST split them across multiple EmailPush objects.

In some cases, just a single Email may be too large. The "properties" array of the associated EmailPushConfig is in priority order: the server MUST add properties to each Email object in this order and, if adding a property would exceed the size limit, the server MUST omit that property and all subsequent properties. The server MUST NOT omit properties from an Email object unless that Email object, alone in an EmailPush, would exceed the size limit. The properties present in each Email object are therefore always a prefix of the requested list. Clients are RECOMMENDED to only request the properties they need for the visible notification, plus the "id" property if they want to then fetch further information, and to list the most important properties first.

Delivery of push messages is not guaranteed: the push service may delay or drop them. Clients MUST NOT rely on EmailPush objects as a complete record of new messages, and should use the normal mechanisms to resynchronise their state (such as "Email/changes", or IMAP if the account does not support urn:ietf:params:jmap:mail).

dl.dd: The state string for the Email data type in this account, as would be returned by an "Email/get" call () made after all of the Emails in the "emails" array were created. If the account does not support the urn:ietf:params:jmap:mail capability, this is null.

If the PushSubscription has an EmailCountConfig for this account (see ), this is an EmailCount object (see ) giving the value of the count after all of the Emails in the "emails" array were delivered. Otherwise, this is null. This allows the client to update a badge at the same time as showing a notification for the new messages. The server MUST include this before adding any properties to the Email objects when calculating the size of the EmailPush object.

section.name: The EmailCount Object
section.t: An EmailCount object gives the current value of a count of the emails in a mailbox, as requested by the client in an EmailCountConfig (see ). It has the following properties:

dl.dd: The id of the Account the mailbox is in.
The value of the requested count property of the mailbox.

The time at which the count had this value. For a given PushSubscription and account, the server MUST ensure the "updated" value of each EmailCount it sends, whether on its own or in an EmailPush object, is later than that of any EmailCount it previously sent; if necessary, it may include fractional seconds to ensure this.

section.t: The server sends an EmailCount object on its own when the value of the count differs from the value it last sent to that PushSubscription for that account, unless it is about to send the new value in the "emailCount" property of an EmailPush object. It MUST also send one with the current value after the PushSubscription is verified, and after the client changes the EmailCountConfig for the account, so the client has an initial value.

A single user action, such as marking many emails as read, may cause many changes to the count in quick succession. To avoid sending a large number of push messages, and so being rate limited by the push service, the server SHOULD wait for a short period after a change, such as a few seconds, before sending an EmailCount object, so that further changes can be combined into a single push. The server MAY further limit the rate at which it sends EmailCount objects, but if the count has changed it MUST eventually send an EmailCount object with the latest value.

Push services may delay, reorder, or drop push messages. Clients MUST ignore an EmailCount object (on its own or in an EmailPush object) if its "updated" value is not later than that of the last EmailCount object they processed for the same account. Clients SHOULD fetch the count directly from the server, for example with "Mailbox/get" or the IMAP STATUS command , when they are next able to, such as when the user opens the app.

Note, some push services and platforms require the client to display a visible notification for every push message it receives. On such platforms, the client may not be able to update its badge silently when it receives an EmailCount object on its own, and will have to rely on fetching the count directly as described above.

section.name: Extension to the PushSubscription Object
section.t: The PushSubscription object is defined in . This document defines two extra properties for this object:

dd.t: If not null, this is a map. The keys are Account ids for accounts with support for the urn:ietf:params:jmap:emailpush capability. The server will push EmailPush objects for these accounts when a new message arrives, in accordance with the associated EmailPushConfig options for the account.

Unlike the "url" and "keys" properties, this property is mutable: the client may update it with "PushSubscription/set" to change which messages are pushed, or set it to null to stop EmailPush objects from being sent.

If not null, this is a map. The keys are Account ids for accounts with support for the urn:ietf:params:jmap:emailpush capability, where the "countProperties" property of the capability is not the empty array. The server will push EmailCount objects for these accounts when the requested count changes, in accordance with the associated EmailCountConfig options for the account.
This property is mutable: the client may update it with "PushSubscription/set" to change which count is pushed, or set it to null to stop EmailCount objects from being sent.

section.t: To get or set the "emailPush" or "emailCount" properties, the client MUST include the urn:ietf:params:jmap:emailpush capability in the "using" property of the request (see ).

EmailPush and EmailCount objects are sent regardless of the value of the "types" property of the PushSubscription; a client that only wants these objects can set "types" to an empty array. As with StateChange objects, the server MUST NOT send any EmailPush or EmailCount objects until the PushSubscription has been verified (see ).

If the user loses access to an account in the "emailPush" or "emailCount" map, or the account no longer supports the urn:ietf:params:jmap:emailpush capability, the server MUST stop sending EmailPush and EmailCount objects for that account and MUST remove that account from both maps. If the mailbox of an EmailCountConfig is destroyed, or the user loses access to it, or the server no longer supports the requested count property, the server MUST stop sending EmailCount objects for that account and MUST remove the account from the "emailCount" map.
EmailPush and EmailCount objects are only sent to the URL of a PushSubscription. They are not sent over an event-source connection () or a WebSocket push channel ().
An EmailPushConfig object has the following properties:

dd.t: A filter to apply to determine which new messages to push an EmailPush object for. The FilterCondition is as defined in . If null, all new messages delivered to the account are pushed.

The filter is evaluated against the message as it is immediately after delivery, including any mailboxes and keywords assigned by delivery-time processing such as Sieve . Subsequent changes to the message, such as moving it to a different mailbox, do not cause an EmailPush object to be sent.

The server MUST support FilterOperator objects with any of the "AND", "OR", and "NOT" operators, nested to at least the depth given by the "maxFilterDepth" property of the urn:ietf:params:jmap:emailpush account capability (see ), and every FilterCondition property listed in the "filterConditions" property of that capability. If the urn:ietf:params:jmap:mail capability is supported for an account, the server MUST support all the FilterCondition properties, and all the nesting of FilterOperator objects, it supports for the "Email/query" method. Otherwise, it MUST support a FilterOperator at the top level of the filter (i.e., a "maxFilterDepth" of at least 1), but there are no FilterCondition properties it is required to support, except as follows.

If the urn:ietf:params:jmap:mail capability is not supported for an account but the server supports IMAP access to the same account with the ObjectID extension , the server MUST support the "inMailbox" FilterCondition property, using mailbox ids discovered via IMAP (the MAILBOXID values). If it supports the "inMailboxOtherThan" FilterCondition property, it MUST also accept these mailbox ids with it.

This minimal set allows a server with an existing IMAP implementation to support this extension as a step towards full JMAP support. Clients MUST check the account capability before using any FilterCondition property, or nesting FilterOperator objects more than one level deep.

The list of properties to include in the "emails" value of the EmailPush object, in priority order. This is the same as the properties argument in "Email/get", as defined in , except that the "bodyValues" property, and any property defined in another JMAP extension that "Email/get" returns only when given additional arguments, are not supported. If empty, each Email object in the EmailPush is an empty object: the client is notified that new messages have arrived, but no further information about them is included. Unlike "Email/get", the "id" property is not included unless it is listed.
If the urn:ietf:params:jmap:mail capability is supported, the server MUST support all the properties it supports for the "Email/get" method. Otherwise, it MUST support the following properties:

ul.li: keywords
from
to
cc
subject
preview
receivedAt
sentAt

dd.t: Additionally, if the server supports IMAP ObjectID , it MUST also support the following properties:

ul.li: id
threadId
mailboxIds

dd.t: The urgency with which to send push notifications containing the EmailPush object when sending over Web Push . The value MUST be an urgency-option, as defined in .

section.t: When creating or updating a PushSubscription, the server MUST reject the change with an "invalidProperties" SetError, including "emailPush" in the "properties" list, if any of the following are true:

ul.li: The change includes "emailPush" and a key in the "emailPush" map is not the id of an account with support for the urn:ietf:params:jmap:emailpush capability.
The "filter" of an EmailPushConfig contains a filter condition the server does not support.
The "filter" of an EmailPushConfig has a depth greater than the "maxFilterDepth" of the urn:ietf:params:jmap:emailpush capability for that account.
The "properties" of an EmailPushConfig contains a property the server does not support, including "bodyValues".
The "urgency" of an EmailPushConfig is not a valid urgency-option.
The "emailPush" property is not null and the "keys" property of the PushSubscription is null. In this case, the "properties" list also includes "keys".

section.t: In addition to "emailPush", the "properties" list MUST include the path to each invalid value, using the same syntax as a key in a PatchObject (see ): "emailPush/{accountId}" if the account id is not valid, or "emailPush/{accountId}/filter", "emailPush/{accountId}/properties", or "emailPush/{accountId}/urgency" if that property of the EmailPushConfig for that account is not valid.

section.name: EmailCountConfig
section.t: An EmailCountConfig object has the following properties:

dl.dd: The id of the mailbox to count emails in. If the urn:ietf:params:jmap:mail capability is supported for the account, this is the id of a Mailbox object. Otherwise, this is the MAILBOXID of the mailbox, as discovered via IMAP with the ObjectID extension ; if the server does not support IMAP access to the account with ObjectID, the "countProperties" property of the urn:ietf:params:jmap:emailpush capability MUST be the empty array for that account.

dd.t: The count to push: one of "totalEmails", "unreadEmails", "totalThreads", or "unreadThreads", with the same meaning as the Mailbox property of that name defined in . This MUST be one of the values supported by the server, as given by the "countProperties" property of the urn:ietf:params:jmap:emailpush capability.

If the urn:ietf:params:jmap:mail capability is not supported for the account, "totalEmails" is the number of messages in the mailbox and "unreadEmails" is the number of messages without the \Seen flag, as returned by the MESSAGES and UNSEEN items of the IMAP STATUS command respectively. IMAP has no concept of threads, so servers without support for urn:ietf:params:jmap:mail will often not support "totalThreads" or "unreadThreads".

The urgency with which to send push notifications containing an EmailCount object on its own when sending over Web Push . The value MUST be an urgency-option, as defined in . Clients SHOULD NOT use "high", as the count may change frequently. An EmailCount object sent in an EmailPush object is sent with the urgency of the EmailPushConfig.

section.t: When creating or updating a PushSubscription, the server MUST reject the change with an "invalidProperties" SetError, including "emailCount" in the "properties" list, if any of the following are true:

ul.li: The change includes "emailCount" and a key in the "emailCount" map is not the id of an account with support for the urn:ietf:params:jmap:emailpush capability, or the "countProperties" property of the capability for that account is the empty array.
The "mailboxId" of an EmailCountConfig is not the id of a mailbox in the account that the user has access to.
The "property" of an EmailCountConfig is not one of the count properties supported by the server for that account.
The "urgency" of an EmailCountConfig is not a valid urgency-option.
The "emailCount" property is not null and the "keys" property of the PushSubscription is null. In this case, the "properties" list also includes "keys".

section.t: In addition to "emailCount", the "properties" list MUST include the path to each invalid value: "emailCount/{accountId}" if the account id is not valid, or "emailCount/{accountId}/mailboxId", "emailCount/{accountId}/property", or "emailCount/{accountId}/urgency" if that property of the EmailCountConfig for that account is not valid.

section.name: Example
section.t: An email client connects to a server over IMAP () and after authenticating, sees the OBJECTID and JMAPACCESS capabilities advertised.

The JMAPACCESS IMAP capability gives it the URL for the JMAP session resource, and guarantees the client can use the same credentials to authenticate that it used for IMAP. The client fetches the JMAP Session object and finds that the following JMAP capabilities are present:

figure.name: The "capabilities" property of a JMAP Session object

section.t: The server doesn't support urn:ietf:params:jmap:mail yet, so the client can't switch over to using JMAP fully instead of IMAP, but it does support urn:ietf:params:jmap:emailpush, so the client can now use JMAP to receive push notifications.

The "accountCapabilities" property of the user's account in the Session object includes the following, so the client knows it may use the "hasKeyword" filter condition, combined with "inMailbox" in a single top-level FilterOperator:

The user has asked the client to notify them of any message delivered to the inbox, plus any message delivered to another mailbox that has the $notify keyword set. The client also wants to show the number of unread emails in the inbox as a badge on its app icon. The client discovers the mailbox id of the inbox over IMAP using ObjectID, then creates a push subscription by making the following API request:

section.t: The server creates the push subscription and immediately pushes a PushVerification object to the client. The client updates the PushSubscription object with this value to validate it as per . With this done, the server will now push an EmailPush object whenever a new message arrives that is delivered to the mailbox with id "674cc240-95db-49ce-a8a2-054f4f733095", or has the "$notify" keyword. It will also push an EmailCount object whenever the number of unread emails in the inbox changes; the first is sent as soon as the subscription is verified. As the "types" property is the empty array, the server will not push any StateChange objects. For example, a message arrives in the inbox and the server pushes the following:

The client updates the badge on its app icon to 1.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: All security considerations of JMAP apply to this specification. Additional considerations are detailed below.

With the push defined in JMAP Core, no user data travels over the push channel, only state strings. The EmailPush object on the other hand contains sensitive user data. As specified in , to ensure confidentiality and integrity of the user's data, the client MUST specify encryption keys when establishing the PushSubscription and ignore any push notification received that is not encrypted with those keys. To ensure this, the server rejects any attempt to set the "emailPush" property on a PushSubscription that does not have encryption keys (see ).

Even when the push message is encrypted, the push service can observe the time at which each EmailPush object is sent and the size of the encrypted payload. This reveals when the user receives messages matching their filter, and may reveal information about the requested properties, such as the length of the subject. Servers MAY mitigate the latter by padding the payload, as supported by the content coding defined in .

Similarly, the time at which each EmailCount object is sent reveals to the push service when the user's mailbox changes. This may include not only when messages arrive, but also when the user reads, moves, or deletes them, and so may indicate when the user is active.
